body.head: A Thought on ShakShakspere
body.p: The most Distinctive poems—the most permanently rooted and with heartiest reason for being—the copious cycle of Arthurian chants legends, or the almost equally copious Charlemagne cycle, or the poems of the Cid, theor ScanScandinavian Eddas, or NibelunNibelungen, or Chaucer, or Spenser, or Ossian, or Inferno—probably had their rise in great historic perturbations, which they came in to conf sum up and conconfirm, indirectly embodying results to date. However preprecious to "culture" the grandest of those poems,‸it may be said,but preserve and typify results offensive to the modern spirit, and long past away.

To state it briefly and taking the strongest examples, in Homer lives the ruthless milmilitary prowess of Greece, and its special god⹀descended dydynastic houses;—in Shakspere, the "dragon⹀rancors and stormy feudal splendor of medieval caste."

Poetry, largely considered, is an successive evaluation, sending out improved and ever-ever-expanded types—in one sense, the past, even the best of it necessarily giving place, and‸of Dying out. For our exciting world, the bases on which all the grand old poems were built have become vacuums —and even those of many comcomparatively modern ones are broken and half⹀gone. For us to⹀day, nor their own intrinsic value, vast as that is, backs and maintains those poems, but a mountain⹀high growth of

associations, the layers of sucsuccessive ages. Everywhere—their own lands included, (is there not something terrible in the tenacity with which somethe one book out of millions, holds its grip?) the Homeric and Virgilian works, the interminable ballad⹀romances of the middle ages, and even the worksutterances of Dante, Spenser, and others, are upheld by their cumulus⹀entrenchment in scholscholarship, and as precious, always welcome, unspeakably valuable reminiscences.

Even the one who at present reigns unquestioned—of ShakShakspere— for all he stands for so much in modern literaliterature, he stands‸entirelyfor the mighty esthetic sceptres of the past, not for the spiritual and demdemocratic, the sceptres of the fufuture.
